title: Diyarbakır Guide: UNESCO Basalt Walls, Hevsel Gardens & Tigris

metaDescription: Explore Diyarbakır's UNESCO basalt walls, Hevsel Gardens, Hasan Paşa Hanı, Great Mosque, Ten-Eyed Bridge, and routes to Mardin and Hasankeyf.
quickAnswer: Diyarbakır anchors Upper Mesopotamia with 5.8 km of UNESCO-listed Roman-Byzantine basalt walls overlooking the Tigris River and Hevsel Gardens. Inside Sur's historic core, walk between Hasan Paşa Hanı, the Great Mosque, and İçkale before pairing the city with Mardin (95 km south) and Hasankeyf in spring or autumn.

body.text: Built from dark volcanic stone quarried off Mount Karacadağ, Diyarbakır feels visually and historically distinct from western Türkiye. Its fortified old town, Sur, preserves layers of Roman, Marwanid, Artukid, and Ottoman stonework above fertile river terraces that have fed the city for millennia. Planning a southeastern itinerary with [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) balances walking routes inside the walls with realistic highway transfers across Mardin, Batman, and Şanlıurfa.
What makes Diyarbakır's Roman-Byzantine basalt walls UNESCO-listed?

Inscribed on the [UNESCO World Heritage List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1488/) in 2015, Diyarbakır's fortifications span roughly 5.8 kilometers around the old city and connect the Inner Castle (İçkale) to the irrigated Hevsel Gardens along the Tigris River. Eighty-two surviving bastions and 63 carved inscriptions document continuous urban defense from late antiquity to the Ottoman era ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/diyarbakir/see)).

The walls stand 11 to 21 meters high and 3 to 5 meters thick, built largely under Roman Emperor Constantius II in the 4th century CE and reinforced by Byzantine, Seljuk, and Artukid rulers. Walk the southern ramparts near Mardin Gate (Mardin Kapı) and Goat Bastion (Keçi Burcu) to see how the dark basalt curtain wall drops straight toward roughly 4,000 decares of orchards and vegetable plots in Hevsel Gardens, which also support dozens of resident and migratory bird species ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/diyarbakir/see)). Inside İçkale, the Diyarbakır Archaeology Museum displays artifacts spanning over 12,000 years around ancient Amida Mound.
What can you see at Hasan Paşa Hanı, Great Mosque and Ten-Eyed Bridge?

Within a 15-minute walk inside Sur, Hasan Paşa Hanı (1572–1575) hosts stone-courtyard breakfasts beneath striped basalt-and-limestone arches, while Diyarbakır Grand Mosque (Ulu Cami) showcases a 12th-century courtyard and a sundial by polymath Al-Jazari ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/diyarbakir/see)). Four kilometers south, the 11th-century Ten-Eyed Bridge (On Gözlü Köprü) spans the Tigris.

Start early at Hasan Paşa Hanı—described by 17th-century chronicler Evliya Çelebi as solid as a castle—for a traditional Diyarbakır breakfast of braided örgü peyniri cheese, clotted cream, and warm flatbread ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/diyarbakir/see)). Step directly across Gazi Caddesi into Ulu Cami, converted after 639 CE and rebuilt in 1091 under Great Seljuk Sultan Malik-Shah I; its courtyard arcades reuse Roman-era Corinthian columns and border the Mesudiye Madrasa. Before dusk, drive or take a short taxi south to On Gözlü Köprü (built in 1065 under the Marwanid dynasty) for tea beside the Tigris as the sun drops behind the basalt ridges.
How do you pair Diyarbakır with Mardin and Hasankeyf?

Diyarbakır sits 95 km (about 1 hour 15 minutes) north of Mardin along the smooth D950 highway, with Roman border garrison Zerzevan Castle and its Temple of Mithras standing halfway along the route ([Go Türkiye](https://goturkiye.com/diyarbakir/see)). Adding Hasankeyf forms a practical 3-to-4-day southeastern triangle via Batman and Midyat.

A clean routing sequence starts by flying into Diyarbakır Airport (DIY), spending two nights exploring Sur, İçkale, and the Tigris waterfront, then driving south with a 90-minute stop at Zerzevan Castle before reaching Mardin's limestone terraces. From Mardin, continue east through Midyat's Syriac monasteries (Mor Gabriel) to Hasankeyf's new museum and Tigris cliffs, returning either to Batman Airport (BAL) or Diyarbakır Airport. Travellers combining western Ottoman heritage such as [Bursa](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) with Mesopotamia usually fly domestically via Istanbul or Ankara to save two full days of driving.

Start walking the basalt walls before 10:00 or after 16:00 to avoid midday glare off dark stone.
Reserve dinner tables in advance for ciğer kebabı (charcoal-grilled lamb liver) or slow-cooked kaburga dolması (stuffed lamb ribs).
Book a driver or rental car with air conditioning if continuing across Mardin, Midyat, and Hasankeyf.

body.text: When is the best season to visit?

April to mid-May and late September through November offer the most comfortable weather in Diyarbakır, with daytime highs between 20°C and 27°C and clear evenings along the Tigris. Summer months (late June through August) routinely exceed 40°C, making midday sightseeing on dark heat-absorbing basalt exhausting.

Spring turns Hevsel Gardens lush green and fills the Tigris with snowmelt, while October brings mild afternoons, pomegranate harvests, and crisp photography light across the walls. Winter (December to February) is cool and quiet—averaging 6°C to 11°C by day with occasional rain—and can work well for museum-focused trips; compare winter conditions nationwide in our [winter travel guide to Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).

faq.q: How many full days do you need in Diyarbakır?
faq.a: Two full days (two nights) cover Sur's basalt walls, İçkale Archaeology Museum, Hasan Paşa Hanı, Ulu Cami, Surp Giragos Armenian Church, Hevsel Gardens, and Ten-Eyed Bridge at an unhurried pace.

faq.q: Is Diyarbakır Airport close to the historic center?
faq.a: Yes. Diyarbakır Airport (DIY) sits roughly 8 km from Sur, taking 15 to 20 minutes by taxi or private transfer with frequent direct flights from Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir.

faq.q: Can you walk on top of the Diyarbakır City Walls?
faq.a: Selected restored bastions and wall sections—including Keçi Burcu (Goat Bastion), Ulu Beden, and areas near İçkale—are open for panoramic views, though not the entire 5.8 km circuit is continuously walkable along the parapet.

faq.q: What is the best food to try in Diyarbakır?
faq.a: Try ciğer kebabı (spiced lamb liver skewers eaten with grilled peppers and flatbread), kaburga dolması (stuffed spiced lamb ribs), meftune (sumac-rich lamb and eggplant stew), and pistachio-filled burma kadayıf for dessert.

faq.q: Should you visit Zerzevan Castle on the way to Mardin?
faq.a: Yes. Zerzevan Castle sits roughly 45 km southeast of Diyarbakır right off the Mardin highway, making it an easy 60-to-90-minute stop without backtracking.

faq.q: Is Hasankeyf still worth visiting after the dam reservoir filled?
faq.a: While the lower medieval valley was submerged, the relocated Artukid monuments, the modern Hasankeyf Museum, cliffside caves, and boat views along the Tigris canyon still pair naturally with Midyat and Mardin.
